The approach follows classic Annapurna trekking country with lodge stays, then transitions to tented high camps and a rewarding glacier summit.

lede: Dhaulagiri (8,167 m) is the seventh-highest peak on Earth — a massive white pyramid visible from Pokhara and the Annapurna region. The expedition follows the northeast ridge with a long trek through remote valleys and extended high-camp rotations.

lede: Dorje Lakpa (6,966 m) dominates the skyline above the Langtang Valley — a striking, technical peak that combines accessible approach trekking with genuine mountaineering on snow and ice. Views extend from Shishapangma to the Ganesh Himal and beyond.

lede: The Everest–Lhotse combination is among the most prestigious objectives in Himalayan mountaineering — two 8000m peaks sharing the Khumbu Icefall, Western Cwm, and South Col approach. Everwander’s dual-summit expedition is designed for experienced high-altitude climbers who want both the world’s highest summit and its formidable neighbor in one carefully paced season.

name: Mt. Everest Expedition

lede: Standing on the summit of Mt. Everest is the defining achievement in mountaineering. Everwander’s expedition follows the classic South Col route through the Khumbu — with meticulous acclimatization, experienced climbing Sherpas, and expedition-grade logistics at every camp.

name: Gyachung Kang Expedition

lede: Gyachung Kang (7,952 m) is the highest peak in the world that is not an 8000er — a massive, often-overlooked summit between Cho Oyu and the Everest massif. The expedition follows a remote glacier approach with long acclimatization, technical high camps, and sweeping views across the entire Khumbu.

name: Dr. Harka Gurung Chuli Expedition

lede: Dr. Harka Gurung Chuli (7,871 m) rises in the wild Gurja Himal region west of Dhaulagiri — a remote, seldom-climbed peak that rewards teams with true expedition solitude. The long approach through quiet valleys and high pastures sets the tone for a serious alpine objective far from the crowded Khumbu.

name: Himlung Himal Expedition

Panoramas of Manaslu and the Peri Himal range.

lede: Himlung Himal (7,126 m) lies in the remote Nar-Phu valley north of the Annapurna Circuit — a less technical 7000m peak that serves as an excellent bridge between trekking peaks and major expeditions. The northwest route is straightforward by Himalayan standards.

name: Island Peak Expedition
facts: Fit trekker; no prior climbing required

lede: Island Peak (Imja Tse, 6,189 m) is the classic introduction to Himalayan mountaineering — a rewarding summit above the Imja Glacier with views of Lhotse, Nuptse, and Everest. The route includes glacier travel, a steep summit headwall, and proper acclimatization through the Khumbu.

name: Mt. Lhotse Expedition
facts: West face via South Col approach
hl: Fourth-highest mountain on Earth at 8,516 m.

Classic trek through Sherpa villages to shared Base Camp.
Experienced climbing Sherpas for high-altitude rotations.

lede: Lhotse (8,516 m) stands immediately south of Everest and shares much of the Khumbu approach — yet its steep Lhotse Face and demanding high camps make it a serious expedition in its own right. Everwander’s Lhotse expedition follows the standard route with meticulous acclimatization and experienced climbing Sherpas.

name: Lobuche East Expedition
hl: Technical trekking peak on the EBC route.
Trek through the classic Khumbu to Lobuche.
Close-up views of the Everest massif from high camp.
Rope, crampon, and ice-axe practice included.

Ascend to high camp with skills training.
Technical summit push on Lobuche East.
Descend to Lukla and fly to Kathmandu.
lede: Lobuche East (6,119 m) rises directly above the Khumbu Glacier near Everest Base Camp — a more technical climb than Island Peak, with steeper ice and rock sections. It pairs perfectly with an EBC trek or as a focused climbing objective.

name: Mt. Manaslu Expedition
hl: Nepal’s eighth-highest and one of fourteen 8000ers.
Trek through the Manaslu Circuit — fewer crowds than Everest.

lede: Manaslu (8,163 m) rises at the heart of the Manaslu Conservation Area — a quieter, more remote alternative to the crowded 8000m peaks. The expedition follows the standard northeast face route with four high camps, long acclimatization, and spectacular Tibetan-influenced culture along the approach.

name: Mera Peak Expedition
facts: Standard north route via high camp
Fit trekker; basic crampon skills helpful
hl: Panorama of Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu, and Kanchenjunga.

lede: Mera Peak (6,476 m) is the highest of Nepal’s trekking peaks — and its summit offers one of the most spectacular panoramas in the Himalaya, with Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu, and Kanchenjunga all visible on a clear day.

name: Pumori Expedition

lede: Pumori (7,161 m) dominates the skyline above Kala Patthar and Gorak Shep — a beautiful, technical peak that offers some of the finest views of Everest. The northwest ridge route demands solid alpine skills and prior high-altitude experience.

name: Saribung Peak Expedition

lede: Saribung (6,346 m) sits in the remote Damodar Himal between Mustang and Nar-Phu — a wild, arid landscape of high plateaus, ancient trade routes, and glacier camps far from the standard trekking circuits. The expedition demands endurance on the approach and solid glacier skills on the mountain.

name: Tharke Kang Expedition

Long trek through one of Nepal’s wildest valleys.
Close-up panoramas of the world’s third-highest peak.
Tibetan Buddhist villages and traditional mountain life.

Flight to Taplejung region and trek toward Olangchung Gola.

Trek out to road head or airstrip and return to Kathmandu.

lede: Tharke Kang (6,757 m) rises in the remote Olangchung Gola region east of Kanchenjunga — a wild, seldom-visited corner of Nepal where Tibetan-influenced villages and long valley treks set the stage for a true expedition. The summit rewards teams with close views of Kanchenjunga and the eastern Himalaya.

name: Classic Bhutan

lede: Our most comprehensive short Bhutan journey — western valleys, fortress dzongs, forested passes, and the unforgettable hike to Tiger’s Nest with time to absorb each destination.

Morning in Thimphu, return to Paro valley.
lede: A compact cultural circuit for travelers with limited time — covering Bhutan’s essential dzongs, valleys, and viewpoints with comfortable pacing and private guiding.

name: Glimpse of Bhutan
hl: Markets, dzongs, and the pace of Bhutanese city life.
Forest roads and mountain viewpoints throughout.
Visa, permits, hotels, and guiding handled for you.

lede: A refined introduction to the Kingdom of Bhutan — Paro’s valley landscapes, Thimphu’s cultural landmarks, and the iconic climb to Tiger’s Nest monastery.

name: Everest Base Camp (North Face)

lede: Approach the world’s highest summit from the Tibetan plateau — a dramatic overland route with gradual altitude gain, curated viewpoints, and the iconic north base camp beneath Everest’s towering north face.

name: Lhasa, Everest & Kailash
hl: Potala Palace, Jokhang Temple, and centuries of living Buddhist heritage.
Witness the north face from curated high-altitude viewpoints.
Journey toward one of the holiest landscapes in Asia.
Permits, vehicles, guides, and pacing managed end-to-end.

Permit processing and final departure preparation.

lede: This comprehensive journey links Tibet’s cultural heart in Lhasa with the north face of Everest and the revered landscapes around Mount Kailash — one of the most spiritually significant routes in the Himalaya.

name: Lhasa & Surrounds by Jeep
hl: Explore Tibet’s most iconic palace and UNESCO heritage site.
Walk the pilgrim circuit at the spiritual heart of Lhasa.
Adjust daily pacing to your interests and energy.
Context-rich commentary from experienced Tibetan guides.

Guided palace visit and Barkhor exploration.
Sera or Drepung Monastery and city viewpoints.

lede: Discover Lhasa and its surrounding valleys by private jeep — ideal for travelers who want cultural depth, comfort, and flexibility without a demanding overland schedule.

name: Namtso Lake Escape

lede: Journey from Lhasa to Namtso Lake — a vast, mirror-bright alpine lake framed by snow peaks and open plateau skies. One of Tibet’s most beautiful natural wonders.

lede: The Trishuli River flows through a dramatic valley between Kathmandu and Pokhara, offering reliable Class II–III rapids that are exciting without being intimidating. It’s the perfect introduction to Himalayan white water — and a brilliant add-on before or after a trek.

name: Bungee Jumping

Turquoise river, sheer cliffs, and a dramatic suspension bridge.

inc: Bungee jump fee and safety equipment
lede: Suspended above the roaring Bhote Koshi River, Nepal’s bungee jump is a rite of passage for adventure travelers. The 160-metre plunge from a steel bridge into a narrow gorge is as visually stunning as it is heart-pounding — with professional operators, medical staff on site, and a safety record built over decades.

name: Tandem Paragliding
hl: Classic cliff take-off with sweeping Himalayan views.

lede: Pokhara is one of the world’s great paragliding destinations. From the Sarangkot launch cliff, tandem flights drift over terraced hillsides, Phewa Lake, and the full Annapurna panorama — often sharing thermals with eagles and other gliders.

name: Annapurna Base Camp Helicopter Tour
hl: Stand inside one of the Himalaya’s most dramatic cirques.

Pokhara or Kathmandu start — matched to your wider Nepal plan.

lede: Soar into the heart of the Annapurna Sanctuary — a natural amphitheatre of 7,000m peaks — and land at base camp for photographs and time on the ground before returning by air.

name: Damodar Kunda Helicopter Tour
hl: Reach a pilgrimage site few travelers ever see.

Long-range flight toward Upper Mustang and Damodar Kunda.

Scenic return with refueling stops as required.
Transfer to your hotel — flexible timing with weather.
lede: Damodar Kunda lies in one of Nepal’s most isolated corners — a cluster of sacred lakes revered in Hindu and Buddhist tradition, near the Tibetan border. This extended helicopter charter is for travelers seeking a genuinely rare pilgrimage experience.

name: Everest Helicopter Day Trip
hl: Unmatched close-up perspectives of Mount Everest and neighboring giants.
Breakfast at one of the world’s highest hotels — weather permitting.

Hotel pickup, airport transfers, and Everwander coordination throughout.
itin: Private transfer from your Kathmandu hotel to the domestic helipad.
Safety briefing and weather check with your flight crew.

Fly back to Kathmandu with continued aerial sightseeing.

exc: Extra waiting time due to weather
lede: Experience the Himalaya’s greatest icon without weeks on the trail. This private helicopter charter flies from Kathmandu to the Everest region, landing at curated viewpoints with time for photographs and a hotel breakfast overlooking the Khumbu.

name: Gosaikunda Helicopter Tour
hl: Land near the sacred alpine lake complex.
One of Nepal’s most important religious sites.
Fly alongside Langtang Lirung and surrounding peaks.
Ideal for a morning excursion from Kathmandu.
itin: Northbound flight into Langtang National Park.
Ground time at the Gosaikunda lake area.
lede: Gosaikunda’s turquoise alpine lakes are a major Hindu pilgrimage destination — traditionally reached by a multi-day trek. This helicopter tour places you beside the sacred waters with time on the ground and sweeping Langtang views.

name: Langtang Valley Helicopter Tour
hl: Fly face-to-face with the dominant peak of the range.
Aerial perspectives over icefalls and high pastures.
Less flight time, more mountain time.
Overfly traditional Tamang villages en route.
itin: Northbound flight over hills into Langtang National Park.

lede: The Langtang Valley lies closer to Kathmandu than any other major Himalayan range — making it ideal for a spectacular half-day helicopter tour over glaciers, alpine meadows, and Tamang heritage villages.

lede: The road to Muktinath is one of Nepal’s great overland journeys — tracing the Kali Gandaki River between Dhaulagiri and Annapurna to a temple revered by both Hindus and Buddhists. This compact six-day drive covers the highlights of Lower Mustang without the restricted-area permit.

The overland journey is an adventure in itself: remote roads, hill villages, and landscapes that feel untouched by time.

Every year thousands of pilgrims climb here for Janai Purnima, bathing in the icy waters and worshipping at the lakeside shrine.

The magnificent Janaki Temple draws pilgrims from Nepal and India year-round, its white marble towers rising above a city alive with devotional song and Mithila art.

lede: Lumbini is among Buddhism’s four holiest sites — the garden where Queen Maya Devi gave birth to Siddhartha Gautama beneath a sal tree. Today the sacred zone spans monasteries built by nations across Asia, the Maya Devi Temple, Ashoka’s pillar, and peaceful canals lined with prayer flags.

lede: Muktinath is one of Nepal’s holiest shrines — a place where Hindus and Buddhists worship side by side beneath the Annapurna massif. The temple complex features 108 sacred water spouts, an eternal flame fed by natural gas, and sweeping views across the Kali Gandaki corridor. This six-day pilgrimage follows the ancient trade route through the world’s deepest gorge.

Trek the classic Annapurna Circuit through Manang’s Tibetan-flavoured villages, cross the formidable Thorong La at 5,416 metres, and descend to Muktinath before switching to 4×4 for the high desert of Upper Mustang — walled Lo Manthang, cave monasteries, and the rain shadow of the Annapurna massif.

lede: This curated fourteen-day journey balances Nepal’s greatest hits without rushing. Begin among Kathmandu’s UNESCO-listed palaces and living temples, then trade city stone for rhododendron ridges on the gentle Ghorepani–Poon Hill circuit — a rewarding introduction to Himalayan trekking with sunrise views of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna. Finish beside Phewa Lake in Pokhara with time for boating, village walks, and optional adventure add-ons.

lede: Australian Camp sits on a ridge at 2,100m with front-row views of Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machapuchare, and Dhaulagiri. The day begins with a drive to Kande, a two-hour ascent to the camp, then a long descent through the Gurung village of Dhampus to Phedi.

lede: Begnas Lake lies east of Pokhara in a bowl of forested hills — quieter than Phewa, popular with locals for boating and picnics. The hike descends from Kalikasthan through Thumakot village and lush countryside to the lakeshore.

lede: The World Peace Pagoda — Shanti Stupa — crowns a forested hill above Phewa Lake’s southern shore. Built to promote world peace, it offers one of Pokhara’s most serene viewpoints: the full Annapurna wall rising above the lake, with Machapuchare dominating the skyline.

lede: Sarangkot rises west of Pokhara — a hill station famed for sunrise, paragliding launches, and unobstructed views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna, and Machapuchare. This day hike drives to Naudanda, then ascends on foot through villages and terraced fields.

lede: Bardia National Park in far-western Nepal is Chitwan’s quieter sibling — larger, less visited, and one of the best places in the country to search for Bengal tigers. Sal forest, grassland, and the Karnali River support rhinos, wild elephants, swamp deer, and over 400 bird species in near-pristine habitat.

lede: Chitwan National Park protects one of Asia’s last strongholds of the greater one-horned rhinoceros — alongside Bengal tigers, sloth bears, gharial crocodiles, and over 500 bird species. This classic 2-night package covers the park’s essential experiences: jeep safari through sal forest and grassland, a quiet canoe drift on the Rapti, a Tharu village walk, and an evening cultural program.

This extended package adds a second full safari day with varied activities — morning jeep drives in different sectors, canoe and riverbank walks, a visit to the elephant and gharial breeding center, and dedicated bird-watching sessions when migratory species fill the wetlands.

lede: For travelers who want Chitwan’s wildlife without sacrificing comfort, Everwander partners with Nepal’s finest jungle lodges — properties with infinity pools, spa treatments, private naturalists, and gourmet dining set against sal forest and river views.
